sources.use: POSIX record locks are released by closing any same-process descriptor for that file; kernel fixture independently reproduces this
SQLite locking context; actual shipped bundled SQLite is exercised in the regression

limits.note: existing component length policy; rollback now participates. Not callback-enforced growth, shared state quota, physical allocation, RSS or a hard kernel deadline

semantics.authority: one retained native directory per opened AuditStore, shared by clones and live claims; no aggregate AuditStore handle admission yet
semantics.identity: relative no-follow metadata for private ordinary single-link files; Linux enforces captured statx mount, Unix requires same native device. Never open/drop another database descriptor for identity or size checks
semantics.absence: only typed NotFound is absent optional sidecar storage; linked, unsafe, denied, provider and uncertain states remain errors
semantics.creation: exclusive relative creation refuses an existing name without opening or truncating it; sync uses admitted retained directory
semantics.defaultVfs: SQLite still opens pathname with its default VFS. Before/after display-root/database metadata gates do not bind the actual C file object, eliminate ABA/final pathname races, or enforce all growth
semantics.macPolicy: shared no-materialization and checked-restoration policy covers native preflight only; default SQLite I/O is not covered by that claim
semantics.windows: audit remains UnsupportedPlatform; Unix-only cache dependency and metadata consumer are properly gated
semantics.records: no permission repair, integrity record eviction, Trash or permanent deletion in this unit
semantics.oracle: fresh exec child uses F_GETLK, bounded 10 seconds, no output pipes and owned-child cleanup. Verify actual SQLite lock survives checks, disappears after close, and independently calibrate old extra-FD-close defect. Child observations excluded from main test counts
